original_question: For a general semi-algebraic set, can the exponent O(k^2) in the complexity of roadmap algorithms be improved to O(k), so that testing connectivity has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness? More broadly, can one design roadmap or connecting-path algorithms whose complexity improvement would also yield sharper effective bounds on the lengths of semi-algebraic connecting paths?
target_in_paper: Section 9 open problem: "More Efficient Algorithms for Computing the Number of Connected Components for General Semi-algebraic Sets ?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's main open question about improving the current roadmap complexity from an O(k^2) exponent to an O(k) exponent, with the explicit goal of making connectivity asymptotically as hard as emptiness; it also correctly picks up the immediately adjacent motivation that better roadmap or connecting-path algorithms would sharpen effective bounds on the lengths of semi-algebraic connecting paths. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))
missing_details: The paper formulates the problem for a P-semi-algebraic set S contained in Z(Q,R^k) := {x in R^k : Q(x)=0}, where R is a real closed field, Q is in R[X_1,...,X_k], P is a finite subset of R[X_1,...,X_k], #P = s, and all degrees are bounded by d. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))
The relevant dimension parameter is k_0 = dim_R Z(Q,R^k) (real dimension), not just the ambient dimension k. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

The current roadmap bound being targeted is the one in Theorem 4.15: s^(k_0+1) d^(O(k^2)) arithmetic operations in the ordered ring D generated by the coefficients of Q and P; if D = Z and the coefficient bit-sizes are bounded by tau, the corresponding bit-size growth is tau d^(O(k^2)). ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

The comparison benchmark is specifically Theorem 4.12, which gives the best single-exponential emptiness/sample-point complexity in this setup; the draft mentions emptiness only informally and does not tie it to that theorem. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

The relevant notion is semi-algebraic connectedness: a roadmap is a semi-algebraic subset M of S of dimension at most 1 such that, for every semi-algebraically connected component D of S, D intersect M is semi-algebraically connected, and every component of every fiber S_x meets M. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

The official heading is about computing the number of connected components for general semi-algebraic sets; 'testing connectivity' is the interpretive consequence stressed in the sentence below the heading, but it is not itself the title of the open problem. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

The path-length discussion is not posed by the paper as a separate broader open problem; it is an immediate motivation/consequence attached to the roadmap-complexity question. In particular, for S contained in the unit ball, Crofton's formula applied to Theorem 4.15 gives a path-length bound of s^(k_0+1) d^(O(k^2)). ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

The comparison with D'Acunto-Kurdyka is narrower than your draft suggests: it concerns two points in a connected component of a real algebraic set in the unit ball defined by degree-d polynomials, proves existence of a semi-algebraic path of length d^(O(k)), and the paper emphasizes that the semi-algebraic complexity of such a path is not bounded in terms of d and k. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))
refined_question: Let R be a real closed field, let Q in R[X_1,...,X_k] be of degree at most d with Z(Q,R^k) := {x in R^k : Q(x)=0} of real dimension k_0, let P be a finite subset of R[X_1,...,X_k] with #P = s and deg(P) <= d for all P in P, and let S be a P-semi-algebraic subset of Z(Q,R^k) (that is, S is defined by a Boolean formula with atoms P=0, P>0, or P<0 for polynomials P in P). Since the best known roadmap algorithm computes a roadmap of S in complexity s^(k_0+1) d^(O(k^2)) (Theorem 4.15), can one improve this to complexity s^(k_0+1) d^(O(k)), so that deciding or counting the semi-algebraically connected components of S has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness in the sense of Theorem 4.12? In the special case that S is contained in the unit ball, can such an improvement also provide the corresponding effective O(k)-exponent bound on the length of semi-algebraic connecting paths, thereby yielding an effective version of the D'Acunto-Kurdyka d^(O(k)) length bound for real algebraic sets? ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))
justification: The draft is not targeting a theorem from the introduction; it is essentially a paraphrase of the Section 9 open problem on general semi-algebraic sets. Its first sentence matches the official question almost verbatim: whether the O(k^2) exponent in roadmap complexity can be reduced to O(k) so that connectivity matches emptiness asymptotically. Its second sentence mirrors the next paragraph, where the paper explains via Crofton's formula that better roadmap or connecting-path algorithms would improve effective bounds on path length, and compares this with the D'Acunto-Kurdyka d^(O(k)) length result whose semi-algebraic complexity is uncontrolled. ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))
